A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same spectral-estimation work. Their main text, equations, seven corresponding figures, and complete appendices support comparison despite extensive notation changes and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original finite-dimensional simulations of eigenvalue distributions and recovery overlaps in Figures 1–7, including averages over ten instances.

after.justification: v2 retains the original eigenvalue and recovery-overlap simulations in Figures 1–7, including the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The two spectral estimators remain equivalent after replacing tensor notation with matrices. However, the auxiliary symmetric GAMP normalization changes from enforcing unit operator norm of V at each iteration to an explicit gamma_t rule targeting unit norm at convergence (v2 Appendix C.1, Eq. 88).

E1.justification: The simulations retain Gaussian multi-index problems with product, squared-norm, sign-product, and ratio link functions. The expanded jointly diagonalizable theory introduces no additional evaluated dataset or task.

E2.justification: Figures 2 and 4 retain the symmetric-versus-asymmetric estimator comparisons and theoretical predictions. Newly cited research, including Kovačević et al., is not added as an experimentally evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The simulations retain their sample-complexity sweeps, eigenvalue and overlap metrics, and sample sizes. For example, Figures 2 and 4 still use n=5000 or d=5000, while Figures 3 and 6 use d=10000; no revised experimental procedure is reported.

E4.justification: The spectral-distribution and recovery-overlap case studies are retained, including the appendix examples. The new appendix material supplies theoretical arguments rather than additional ablations, robustness tests, or empirical supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Figures 4 and 7 still report averaging over ten instances. The plotted uncertainty presentation is retained, with no added run counts, seed information, confidence-interval procedure, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Figures 1–7 retain their simulation points, curves, and reported thresholds, including approximately 0.59375 for the product example and 2 for the four-dimensional squared-norm example. The explicit statement that lambda_s=1 formalizes the value already depicted; no changed empirical performance is reported.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 3.11 and the Appendix C.3 random-matrix argument for the jointly diagonalizable case, which v1 only proposed formalizing. It also adds conjecture sketches in Appendices C.2 and D, revises stability reasoning, corrects the squared-norm scaling in Definition 2.1, and reverses the erroneous moment inequality in v1 Eq. 153 through v2 Eq. 175. The general spectral statements remain conjectures.

C1.justification: The abstract, main-contributions paragraph, and conclusion retain the same central claims: two AMP-inspired spectral estimators achieve the optimal weak-recovery threshold without informed initialization and exhibit a BBP-like transition. The additional theorem supplies supporting theory without redefining these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 makes logarithmic-iteration convergence assumptions explicit and distinguishes established special cases from the conjectural general setting. Appendices B.1 and F also discuss additional informative eigenvectors, including an informative subspace hidden inside the asymmetric operator's spectral bulk.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly provides an explicit gamma_t selection formula, replacing the earlier implicit normalization prescription. Experimental implementation information and code, data, and hardware disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of independent work by Kovačević et al. and positions it as providing an alternative special-case analysis. It also adds Rush and Venkataramanan, Li and Wei, and Li et al. to support the longer-iteration AMP discussion. Other changes, such as Troiani's publication update, concern existing references.

P1.justification: The exposition replaces tensor-specific definitions throughout with explicit matrix and vec/mat notation, rewrites algorithm and proof presentations, and compresses Section 4's numbered subsections into example lists. The appendices are reorganized around separate theorem arguments and conjecture sketches, substantially changing the technical presentation.

P2.justification: All seven figures are retained with the same graphical results. Changes include resizing and repositioning Figure 2, placing Figures 5 and 6 on separate pages, caption refinements such as lambda_s=1 in Figure 3, and more compact equation layouts.

improvement.justification: v2 improves exposition, corrects mathematical statements, and adds substantial special-case theory. However, new Lemma C.5 has a Schur-complement sign inconsistency with the block matrix in Eq. 121, while Appendices C.2 and D infer O(log d) convergence from a gap condition that permits a vanishing gap. These unresolved steps weaken the principal added theoretical support. With empirical evidence unchanged, the benefits and mathematical reliability concerns do not establish a clear net quality improvement.
